why: rcl_action exposes the action's three services and two topics one message at a time so a caller can drive the protocol itself. Ours runs the protocol inside the executor's action arena and hands the user the DECISIONS (accept/reject, cancel accept/reject) and the payloads; the part a caller may drive is the L1 polling tier (`nros_action_server_try_recv_goal_request_raw`, `nros_action_client_send_goal_raw`, ...), which is RFC-0022's polling tier for actions -- see the pubsub stage's `cpp:PollingSubscription`. and the payload is CDR bytes (`const uint8_t*, size_t`) rather than rcl's `void* ros_message`, because the C ABI has no runtime typesupport -- the only publish in the whole C surface is `rclc_publish_raw`. See the pubsub stage's `c:publish_raw` and `c:message_type_t`.
